motivating_context: S20 H1 (order block + OI confirmation, patient exit) is the best-validated strategy in this project (PF 1.066 development, 1.117 validation, both base costs) but fails validation stress (PF 0.857 < 1.00). Four subsequent attempts to fix this by changing EXECUTION (S19 earlier breakeven, S21/S21c limit entry, S22 larger size) all made results worse, not better. None of those touched WHICH candidates get traded. This protocol tests the one remaining, previously untried lever: taking fewer, more convicted candidates by raising the existing regime/structure thresholds already built into order_block_oi_confirmation_scalp.py — not inventing a new composite score (which would risk being tuned to this data), just raising two knobs that already existed with principled, round-number values.

hypotheses.entry_exit: identical to S20 H1 (order_block_oi_confirmation_scalp, route='oi', partial_r=1.5, trail_atr=2.5, target_r=8.0) EXCEPT adx_threshold raised to 30.0 (was 20.0) — a materially stronger, pre-declared round-number conviction bar on the regime confirmation, not tuned by scanning multiple values against this data
identical to S20 H1 EXCEPT displacement_atr_mult raised to 2.5 (was 1.5) — a materially stronger, pre-declared round-number conviction bar on the order-block displacement itself

single_variable_isolated: H1 changes only adx_threshold versus S20 H1. H2 changes only displacement_atr_mult versus S20 H1. Everything else (entry structure logic, flow/OI confirmation, stop placement, exit management, position sizing) is byte-for-byte identical to S20 H1 in both.
why_these_two_values_and_not_a_grid: 30.0 and 2.5 are round-number, roughly 1.5x-1.67x increases over S20's 20.0/1.5 — chosen before looking at any result from this protocol, not selected from a swept range. Only these two, pre-declared, single-variable changes are tested; no other threshold combination is tried.

symbols.note: Reuses the exact same cached klines/funding/metrics archives already downloaded for S18/S20 — no new data source.

promotion_gates.development_to_validation: PF >1.05, net PnL >0, at least 40 fills
promotion_gates.validation_to_retrospective_evaluation: base PF >1.10, stress PF >=1.00, at least 20 base fills, at least 2/3 symbols net positive, no symbol >60% gross profit
promotion_gates.paper_to_live: at least 200 prospective candidates across three full frozen months, PF >=1.25 base and >=1.10 stress, expectancy >=0.10R, 95% session-block bootstrap lower bound >0, max DD <=4%

execution.one_global_position: single global minute event loop with one shared cash balance, pending order and open position across the correlated ETH/SOL/BNB cluster
execution.ambiguous_bar: stop first; no favorable exit on limit fill minute

selection: Exactly H1 and H2. Both may plausibly fall below the 40-fill development minimum given the tighter thresholds — that is a legitimate, disclosed possible outcome of this protocol, not grounds to loosen the bar afterward. A failing gate stops that route; choose no least-bad winner.
stress_semantics: Stress and severe are deployability replays: higher costs and limit penetration are known before entry, so the reward/cost filter is reapplied and the fill cohort may shrink.
known_limitations: Fewer candidates could fall below statistically meaningful sample size even if the per-trade PF genuinely improved — the 40/20-fill minimums in the promotion gates exist precisely to guard against over-interpreting a small, lucky sample.
Same order-block, OI, ATR-freeze and no-order-book-reconstruction simplifications as S18/S20.
This is a retrospective diagnostic; not a live paper-forward result.
